best_practices: Plan site structure, sitemap, and content hierarchy before opening the WordPress editor.
Use native Gutenberg core blocks and block themes for fast, clean, maintainable websites.
Optimize and compress all images before uploading to maintain fast page load times.
Enforce strong passwords and limit administrator privileges to essential users only.
Configure automated, off-site backups before updating WordPress core, themes, or plugins.
Test website navigation, forms, and readability on real mobile devices before launch.
Create dedicated Editor accounts for clients rather than sharing master Administrator access.
Document maintenance procedures, update schedules, and support contacts in a client guide.
common_mistakes: Installing dozens of overlapping plugins that slow down site speed and introduce security vulnerabilities.
Using heavy legacy page builders when native block themes can achieve clean layouts with superior performance.
Uploading multi-megabyte uncompressed images directly from cameras or stock photo websites.
Ignoring mobile responsiveness and only checking page designs on widescreen desktop monitors.
Failing to configure automated backups, risking complete data loss during server or update crashes.
Leaving default 'admin' usernames, weak passwords, and insecure login endpoints exposed.
Changing URLs after launch without redirects, resulting in broken links and 404 indexing errors.
Handing over a website to a client without documentation or instructions on how to edit content safely.

faq.question: Can beginners learn WordPress without coding?
faq.answer: Yes. This course starts with website planning and WordPress fundamentals, then teaches practical website creation using Gutenberg and modern block themes. Advanced programming is not required.

faq.question: What will I build during the course?
faq.answer: You will complete a five-page business website containing Home, About, Services, Blog and Contact pages, along with essential functionality, basic SEO and client handover documentation.

faq.question: Is Elementor included?
faq.answer: The course focuses primarily on WordPress Gutenberg and the Site Editor. Advanced Elementor page building belongs to the separate Elementor specialization.

faq.question: Will I learn WooCommerce?
faq.answer: No. This course covers general WordPress website design and management. WooCommerce store creation is covered separately in Course 63.

faq.question: Will I learn WordPress SEO and security?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn foundational SEO, website performance checks, access security, backups and essential maintenance practices.

faq.question: Can I use these skills for freelance projects?
faq.answer: The course teaches practical capabilities applicable to beginner-level business website projects and website maintenance services. Client acquisition and income are not guaranteed.

faq.question: What is the duration and course fee?
faq.answer: The course includes 48 guided learning hours delivered over six weeks. The listed course fee is ₹6,900, subject to the website's verified pricing and tax policy.

faq.question: What is the difference between WordPress and Elementor?
faq.answer: WordPress is the content management system used to manage websites. Elementor is a visual page-building tool used with WordPress. This course prioritizes native block-based WordPress design; advanced Elementor workflows are taught separately.

faq.question: What computer software or hardware do I need to get started?
faq.answer: You need a computer running Windows, macOS, or Linux with at least 8 GB of RAM and an active internet connection. We use LocalWP, a free and reliable local staging environment, so you do not even need to purchase hosting immediately to start learning.

faq.question: What is the difference between WordPress.com and WordPress.org?
faq.answer: WordPress.org provides the free, open-source WordPress software that you install on your own web hosting or local environment, giving you complete ownership, freedom, and administrative control. WordPress.com is a hosted commercial service with plan restrictions. This course focuses entirely on self-hosted WordPress (WordPress.org standards).

faq.question: Why does Nova Skills focus on Gutenberg and modern block themes rather than classic themes?
faq.answer: WordPress has transitioned to Full Site Editing (FSE) and native block themes (such as Twenty Twenty-Four). Block themes are faster, cleaner, more accessible, and adhere directly to modern web standards without requiring bloated external page-builder plugins or paid annual licenses.

faq.question: How will I learn to handle website backups and disaster recovery?
faq.answer: In Module 05, you will configure automated scheduled backups using industry-standard tools like UpdraftPlus. You will practice creating full backups of both the database and file system, storing them in external cloud storage, and testing backup restoration.

faq.question: How does AI fit into this WordPress course?
faq.answer: AI tools can assist with drafting initial text, structuring sitemaps, generating meta descriptions, and outlining client documentation. However, you will learn strict human verification protocols to ensure factual accuracy, brand voice alignment, design hierarchy, and security before publishing.

faq.question: What is included in the Client Handover deliverable?
faq.answer: The client handover package includes creating restricted user accounts (Editor roles) for the client, compiling a step-by-step maintenance handbook, providing backup schedule documentation, detailing recommended plugin update procedures, and conducting a recorded walkthrough demonstration.

faq.question: Will I receive a certificate upon completing the program?
faq.answer: Yes. Upon completing all six curriculum modules, successfully building and testing the five-page business website, and submitting the client handover documentation with a passing score of at least 70%, you receive the verified Nova Skills Certificate of Completion in WordPress Website Design & Management.
